title_guess: NEER vs REER: measuring the rupee against a basket of currencies

segments.teaches: prices of everyday goods and services keep moving up and down

elements.what: grid of flat green icons (house, food items, bus, medicine, bottle, graduate, fuel and others)
stacked green chevrons or red down-arrows on each icon, changing continuously

segments.notes: Continuous ambient animation (no settled frame) shows prices fluctuating.

segments.teaches: to know whether general prices are rising we use two indexes, CPI and WPI, each a weighted average of price changes of a basket

elements.what: light-blue panel slides in behind the icon grid
blue question box under an INFLATION heading
'2 INDEXES' splitting to CPI and WPI with full names
small basket pictures beside CPI (goods) and WPI (sacks and crates)
note: indexes are weighted averages over a basket (key words bold)

segments.notes: Inflation indexes used as the familiar analogy for currency indexes.

segments.teaches: in the same way, to know whether our currency is rising or falling against all other currencies we need indexes

elements.what: inflation question and its '2 INDEXES -> CPI / WPI' moved up into a compact row
mint-green panel across the lower half
white question box about the currency, with an arrow to a faded '2 indexes' placeholder

segments.notes: Parallel structure: the new question mirrors the old one, and the answer is left faded to be filled later.

segments.teaches: India trades with many countries, so the rupee has many exchange rates

elements.what: globe on the left
maroon India silhouette on the right
fan of curved black arrows from the globe converging on India

segments.notes: Arrows draw on continuously for about 15 s.

segments.teaches: tracking every currency is impractical, so we need an index; two exist, NEER and REER, built on a weighted basket of the currencies we trade with most

elements.what: cream box under a black rule: cannot track all rates
down-arrow to a second statement
hand-drawn ellipse around the word 'index', later filled yellow
arrows from 'index' to two yellow tags NEER and REER
wicker basket of banknotes with a caption
countries (USD, JPY, CNY, GBP, EUR, HKD) in a blue column with weights 30/20/20/10/10/10

segments.notes: Earlier statements fade to grey when the table arrives (dim-the-old, show-the-new).

segments.teaches: NEER is the weighted sum of the rupee's nominal exchange rates: weight x rate for each currency, added up (0.26849 in the example)

elements.what: basket at the table corner and a rupee sign over the rate column
countries x weight x exchange rate (1 Rs = ...) x working ('30% of 0.012') x results; results column highlighted blue
row arrows into the results and a down-arrow to the total
yellow NEER tag under the total 0.26849

segments.notes: Same worked-table pattern as E05 with different numbers.

segments.teaches: reading NEER: 0.26849 units of the basket equal one rupee; NEER up means the rupee appreciated, NEER down means it depreciated

elements.what: 0.26849 (NEER tag) x basket = rupee sign, in a light-blue band
rounded red box (NEER rises) and blue dotted box (NEER falls) under underlined headings

segments.notes: Condition-box pair identical in style to E05.

segments.teaches: REER uses real exchange rates instead: the nominal rate adjusted for inflation, then the same weighted sum

elements.what: NEER tag, basket, rupee sign and the total scatter, then fly back into table positions
the NEER table rebuilt with an extra REAL exchange rate column header; exchange-rate column tinted green
cream box: real exchange rate = nominal exchange rate / ((1 + inflation)/100)
yellow ellipse 'REAL exchange rate' over the column
curved arrow from the ellipse to the working column, whose rate values get yellow highlights

segments.notes: Morph transition: pieces of the previous formula fly into the rebuilt table. Shows REER as a one-column change to the NEER method.

segments.teaches: comparing NEER and REER: NEER is the weighted average of nominal rates (no inflation adjustment)

elements.what: yellow NEER and REER tags
large italic VS between the tags
pink definition box for NEER

segments.teaches: closing comparison between the two indexes

elements.what: NEER and REER tags kept
VS replaced by a large comparison sign (<)
app promo overlay at bottom left

segments.notes: Symbol swap carries the conclusion; the definition box is removed.

elements.what: next-video and playlist panels
